plan.name: Post-MI Introductory Reconditioning — 2-Week Starter Block
plan.description: A conservative 2-week introductory programme for a 58-year-old male, 6 months post-myocardial infarction, cleared by cardiac rehab for moderate-intensity exercise only. Heart rate capped at 115 bpm (~70% age-predicted max). No Valsalva, no maximal lifts. Full gym available.

goals.name: Safe cardiovascular reconditioning
goals.description: Re-establish aerobic base while keeping HR below 115 bpm at all times.

goals.name: Rebuild foundational muscular endurance
goals.description: Restore whole-body muscular endurance using light loads, controlled tempo, and open-glottis breathing.

actions.note: Reduce cardio target HR ceiling by 10 bpm and drop resistance sets by 1 if sleep < 6 h.
Convert next scheduled training day to active_recovery if yesterday RPE >= 7.

phases.name: Introductory Reconditioning
phases.description: Two weeks of low-to-moderate intensity work. Establish movement patterns, breathing discipline (no breath-holding), and aerobic base. HR must remain ≤115 bpm throughout. RPE target 3–5 on 1–10 scale.

checkpoints.name: End of Week 1 Check-in
questions: Any chest pain, palpitations, or unusual shortness of breath during sessions?
Did HR stay below 115 bpm throughout all sessions?
Rate your overall energy levels this week (1–10).
Any joint discomfort or muscular pain to report?

checkpoints.name: End of Week 2 — Baseline Assessment

measurements.note: 6-minute walk test on flat surface — monitor HR throughout, stop if HR exceeds 115 bpm.

questions: Any cardiac symptoms (chest tightness, dizziness, palpitations) during or after exercise?
Has your GP or cardiologist been informed of your exercise programme?
How confident do you feel progressing to the next phase?
Rate sleep quality over the past 2 weeks (1–10).

notifications.message: HR monitor alert: if your heart rate exceeds 115 bpm, reduce pace or resistance immediately and allow HR to recover below 100 bpm before continuing.
STOP exercise immediately and seek medical attention if you experience chest pain, pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or palpitations.
Breathing reminder: exhale on exertion, inhale on the easier phase. Never hold your breath during any exercise.
Week 1 complete — time for your check-in. Log your resting HR, RPE, and answer the check-in questions before your next session.
